§6Nitric Acid§f §aCorrosive, oxidizing, and absolutely necessary for explosives and rocket fuel.§f §bNitric Acid§f (HNO3) is a strongly corrosive, polluting liquid (NFPA 3/0/2, OX) used in explosives, rocket propellant, nitroglycerin production, and bedrock ore cleaning. §6Production§f:
§b• Chemical Plant§f (2.5s, 100 HE/t), 500 mB Sulfuric Acid + 1× Niter → 1,000 mB §eNitric Acid§f
§b• Blueprint: Air§f (10s, 5 kHE/t), 8,000 mB Compressed Air + 2,000 mB Water → 1,000 mB §eNitric Acid§f
§b• Industrial Mixer§f, 500 mB Sulfuric Acid + Niter → 1,000 mB Nitric Acid
§b• Industrial Liquefaction§f, Niter → 750 mB Nitric Acid §6Key Uses§f:
§b• §eTATB§f, Chemical Plant: Sour Gas + 10 mB Nitric Acid + TNT
§b• §eSolid Rocket Fuel§f, Petroleum Gas + 100 mB Nitric Acid + 2 Solid Fuel → 4 Rocket Propellant
§b• §eNitroglycerin§f, Industrial Mixer: Petroleum Gas + Nitric Acid + Fish Oil
§b• §eChlorocalcite Solution§f, 250 mB Nitric Acid + 250 mB Water + Chlorocalcite §ePS:§f The Blueprint: Air route eats power (5 kHE/t) but skips niter entirely. Use the Chemical Plant for smaller batches, the Air route when you need volume.
